differences: Experiment 1: the paper's 'average of 22%' of no-movement triplets with speech on the middle trial is the median across participants here (22.2%); the mean is 23.4%.

Experiment 2: the paper gives 127-140 analysed no-movement triplets per participant (median 137); the rows give a median of 137 but a range of 27 to 144, which fits the paper's own 0-115 excluded triplets (144 - 115 = 29).

Standard errors of the model means, some contrasts and some d values are truncated or differ by one unit of the last printed digit in the paper (SE 0.884 is printed 0.8, d 0.248 is printed 0.24, d 0.254 is printed .256, a contrast of 2.45 is printed 2.5), so they are checked to one unit of the last printed digit; every t statistic agrees to its printed decimals.
